rev6.release_notes: Continue Pattern: a zig-zag (X back and forth while Z steps down) continues exactly as typed - each line keeps its own X and the Z keeps its step - to the limit you set.

cadcam.release_notes:
NHP 5500 post: each side's B index is written with its work offset (G00 G54 B0 / G00 G55 B180. ...), set by the new B index row in the Setup window; a post that can't write B refuses a side off B0 instead of posting it at the wrong side.
Post Process: Program for "All setups in order" writes the whole job as one program - every tool on top, a header per side, M00 between sides, M30, then every subprogram (Rev 7 and NHP 5500 posts).
NHP 5500: a 2D Contour's depth passes are one M98 P.. L.. call; the subprogram steps Z by G91, cuts the path and returns to its start (only where that return stays in metal already cut).
Stepdowns: a depth that is a whole number of steps is cut in exactly that many (1.6 at .025 = 64 passes, was 65 at .0246).
Slot: a Zig-zag choice ramps end to end down the centre line, then one flat pass on the floor.
2D Contour: leads move to a Links tab with a Lead type (Angle / Tangent / Extend); Extension moves to Strategy - Geometry.
Milling toolpaths: a Depth tab with Starting Z and Ending Z.
Stock: a body picked as the stock is drawn alone (no box), and Z0 / Simulate follow it when it changes; the STEP's as-turned stock can be the setup's stock; a stock body's faces can be deleted or simplified without touching the part.
Setup window: Stock shape comes first, then Stock type; one set of axis lines (the work zero), half as thick.
Side setups: listing walls no longer fails on a section a hair off level.
Sketch: a rule added to a sized line keeps its length; redraws with many dimensions are about a quarter faster.
